extracted.intended_audience: CIA senior managers and staff responsible for agency management reporting (Inspector General, Executive Director‑Comptroller, Deputy Directors, Office of Planning/Programming/Budgeting, Director of Finance, Information Processing Board, Director of Personnel)
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit the agency management improvement report required by OMB Circular A‑44, organized into the specified sections (I–VIII), assigning responsibility for each section, and meeting OMB deadlines. Includes consolidation of several prior reporting requirements into a single multi‑section submission and preparation of implementing instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of overall responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph seven requires that overall responsibility for the coordination of an Agency's management review and improvement program be delegated to a top-level official reporting directly to the Department or Agency Head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memo suggests assigning this responsibility to either the Inspector General or the Executive Director‑Comptroller. This office will coordinate the entire program, make assignment decisions, and ensure implementing instructions are prepared once the Agency Head decides allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of prior reporting requirements into one submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular consolidates the annual reporting requirements contained in several other OMB documents (old Circular A‑44 on Management Improvement; Reports Reduction reporting requirements; the Financial Management Improvement Program; automatic data processing accomplishments and improvements) into 'one report'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although called 'one report', it is more accurately eight reports (Sections I–VIII) submitted at one time; guidance should address how to integrate previously separate reports into the combined structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section I — Management Reviews (content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section I — Management Reviews: a summary report which includes description of the procedures utilized by the Agency to conduct management reviews; review plans for the upcoming/current year; and a report of the accomplishments and achievements of the review program for the past fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memo recommends the Inspector General as the logical office to assume responsibility for preparing this section and for actions envisioned under Sections I and II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section II — Priority Improvement Projects (content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section II — Priority Improvement Projects: a report of the projects under way or to be undertaken to improve a Government operation or program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspector General is cited as the logical owner for this section's preparation and follow‑up action; should describe project scope, status, and intended improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section III — Financial Accomplishments and Plans (content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section III — Financial Accomplishments and Plans: similar to the current financial management improvement report, possibly in a more summary form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director of Finance (currently responsible for preparing the Financial Management and Improvement Report) can retain responsibility for Section III and should present accomplishments and plans in summary form appropriate to OMB's consolidated submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section IV — Automatic Data Processing (ADP) Improvements (content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section IV — Automatic Data Processing Improvements — in two parts covering (1) improvements in the performance level of programs or activities resulting from the use of ADP and (2) significant improvements in the management of computer facilities and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Information Processing Board is identified as the logical body to assume responsibility for preparing the ADP Improvement Report; the section should separate program performance benefits from facility/resource management improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section V — Management of Federal Reports / Reports Reduction (content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section V — Management of Federal Reports: essentially a report of the Agency's efforts to reduce costs of reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If limited to administrative management reports, the DDS is the logical place for this report. If the Agency elects to include substantive intelligence and operations reports, each Deputy Director should report accomplishments in his Directorate for consolidation by Office of Programming, Planning, and Budgeting (PPB) or the Inspector General. The memo notes uncertainty/recommendation is needed on scope (administrative vs substantive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section VI — Productivity Improvements (content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section VI — Productivity Improvements: covering plans for the current year as well as achievements in the past year by program, project, or function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Productivity measurement and reporting 'impact directly on each Deputy Director'; Deputies should be assigned responsibility for productivity measurement in their directorates and report accomplishments accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section VII — Cost Reductions (content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section VII — Cost Reductions: the establishment of cost reduction and savings goals for the upcoming/current year and those achieved during the past year together with a report on the disposition (e.g., reprogramming or returning to the reserve) of savings achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the Agency's management philosophy, this is a responsibility of the respective Deputy Director; reports should state goals, achieved savings, and how savings were disposed of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section VIII — Nominations for Presidential Management Improvement Awards (content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section VIII — Nominations for the Presidential Management Improvement Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations should be made by each Deputy Director and consolidated by the Director of Personnel for inclusion in Section VIII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on inclusion of substantive intelligence/operations material for Reports Reduction (scope decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: The memo raises a decision point: whether Section V (Reports Reduction) should include substantive intelligence and operations reports as well as administrative management reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If substantive reports are included, each Deputy Director must report accomplishments for consolidation (by PPB or IG); if not, DDS handles the administrative report. This decision affects assignment of responsibility and consolidation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of preparers and implementing instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the Agency Head decides how to allocate responsibility under Circular A‑44, either the Inspector General or the Office of Planning, Programming, and Budgeting can prepare the necessary implementing instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memo calls for prompt issuance of instructions because of the OMB deadline; implementing instructions should specify responsibilities, formats, and schedules for each section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline / timeliness for first report
rubrics_metrics.description: The first report under this Circular is due in OMB by September 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of this fixed deadline, the memo advises issuing implementing instructions 'fairly soon' to allow offices time to compile the multi‑section submission.
